results.title: A Scalable System Architecture for CubeSat Test & Evaluation for Enhanced Mission Success
results.abstract: This research applies systems engineering methodology to optimization of a CubeSat Test and Evaluation program. Currently, over 50% of CubeSats fail to perform their intended mission, in large part, due to inadequate test and evaluation procedures prior to flight. This paper applies Systems Engineering principles to increase the robustness and effectiveness of CubeSat test and evaluation with the goal of reducing the failure rate of CubeSat missions. This paper builds upon previous research to build the scalable systems architecture. The paper covers the set of model-based systems engineering diagrams and reports for the operational and logical/functional viewpoints of the CubeSat Test and Evaluation System.

results.title: Digital Engineering for Cubesats With Semantic Web Technologies
results.abstract: Digital Engineering (DE) and the digital thread, which integrates information across the system lifecycle, offer transformative opportunities for systems engineering. This paper explores the application of DE principles to cubesat design and development, leveraging the Digital Engineering Factory (DEF) developed at the University of Arizona. The DEF integrates data from multiple engineering tools into a cohesive dataset using the Violet tool, which organizes the data as a graph database aligned with the University of Arizona Ontology Stack (UAOS). We extend prior work by applying the DEF to a cubesat design project. In particular, we develop a Python-based analysis to simulate orbital decay and calculate the time required for the cubesat to deorbit. This analysis uses inputs from multiple sources and is integrated into the workflow to demonstrate how the DEF supports automated traceability and checking of consistency, correctness, and completeness. This paper details the DEF's architecture, the cubesat application, and key findings, providing a pathway for advancing DE practices in cubesat design and development. Limitations and future research directions are discussed to guide further development of semantic web technologies in DE.

results.title: Model-Based CubeSat Flight-Software Architecture using a Docs-as-Code approach
results.abstract: View Video Presentation: https://doi.org/10.2514/6.2023-1126.vidWith the growing community of CubeSat developers has emerged a need for a technical approach that would provide a means of fast-tracking the lifecycle development process of CubeSats, including the need to minimize design and development time repeating prior engineering efforts. In addition to a technical approach, there is also the need for a language and toolchain with a demand for both minimal training and minimal IT overhead to configure. A model-based approach has become a topic of interest in addressing much of these systems engineering painpoints. However, the current state-of-the-art tools demand either considerable investment in training and/or IT overhead, making it difficult for CubeSat developers of small startups or academia to participate. This article presents a model-based technical approach in conjunction with a docs-as-code approach, used to fascilitate flight software architecture development, intended to guide an implementation, for the SeaLion CubeSat mission - a joint CubeSat mission between the Old Dominion University and Coast Guard Academy. The technical approach discussed in this paper was also used to model and generate the paper as itself.

results.title: EarthScan-TSS, a Cubesat Based Tethered Satellite System And Platform To Test On Orbit Servicing And Space Sustainability
results.abstract: View Video Presentation: https://doi.org/10.2514/6.2023-1881.vidIn late 2026, sci_Zone in partnership with John Hopkins University is planning to deploy in Low Earth Orbit the EarthScan-TSS satellite to test on orbit servicing and space sustainability for the DoD, NASA and a range of commercial applications. The focus of the mission is to flight qualify a range of sensors and supporting software, Artificial Intelligence, and Autonomy tools ? QuickSAT/VMS and SHERLOCK MD ? that supports vehicle servicing and fault management, extravehicular assessment, local and global situational awareness and secondary vehicle characterization. The architecture will track data in an on board data lake using a hybrid Trustless Ledger System. For ease of payload repurposing EarthScan-TSS will utilize the flight qualified QuickSAT/Xen Space Hypervisor, a bare metal hypervisor that provides for secure isolation and protection of virtual payloads installed on on-orbit vehicles. QuickSAT/Xen also allows for payload repurposing isolated from the rest of the flight management system. The first phase of the mission is for two years in LEO at an altitude of 600 km to exercise a range of mission goals including a broad range of servicing and autonomy functions. The second phase of the mission will be to deploy a 24U cubesat from the main satellite on a 2 km tether to test a range of secondary vehicle monitoring functions over the controlled deployment and tether operations phases. We will also conduct a de-orbit maneuver using sci_Zone?s proprietary tether design and tether deployer system. For this presentation the mission design will be presented along with the baseline satellite design including both the primary and secondary elements plus the tether system. We will also cover the architecture of the QuickSAT/VMS system, SHERLOCK MD, and QuickSAT/Xen.

results.title: Using Small Satellites to Construct an In-Space Test Platform for Risk Reduction
results.abstract: View Video Presentation: https://doi.org/10.2514/6.2023-2214.vidTo overcome the technical readiness levels (TRL) 4 ? 7 ?Valley of Death? and accelerate new technology development, the US Space Force (USSF) started an in-Space Developmental Test (iSDT) initiative with its instantiation of a persistent iSDT platform called the Advanced Space-Based Testbed (XST). For risk-reduction, a scaled-down Mini-XST is proposed for proof-of-concept. Its key space systems include the spacecraft bus, test payloads, tender servicer to deliver test payload to the Mini-XST spacecraft, and robotic servicer to attach test payloads to the Mini-XST platform. In this paper, the proposed Mini-XST taking advantage of recent proliferated small satellite technologies as well as standard interface to support its successful operation will be discussed and illustrated.

results.title: Digital Engineering Development in an Academic CubeSat Project
results.abstract: Digital engineering is increasingly introduced for managing and supporting the development of systems for space. However, few academic teams have the competency needed to manage projects using digital engineering and systems engineering. The subject of this paper is an academic CubeSat project in which a variety of digital engineering techniques are used. The tailoring that has been applied to fit the academic environment including students from different disciplines and levels of maturity is described. This paper shows how a customized Scrum methodology for hardware and software integrated with a workflow in a digital tool environment has given positive results for both the team and the system development. This paper also discusses how to introduce new members to the team and how to train them to work with digital engineering as a multidisciplinary team. This paper presents how the systems engineering and project management activities have been integrated into the academic CubeSat project, evaluate how well this fusion worked, and estimate its potential to be used as a guide for other digital engineering projects.

results.title: Programmatic Management for the ABEX CubeSat in a Model Based System Engineering Environment
results.abstract: View Video Presentation: https://doi.org/10.2514/6.2021-0623.vidThis paper describes how the systems engineering team has applied a Model Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) methodology to the Alabama Burst Energetics eXplorer (ABEX) project, formerly known as the Alabama Experiment for In-situ Shielding (AEGIS). The MBSE approach is based around the development of an Integrated Systems Model (ISM) that contains a model of the system and most of the programmatic information about the project. This paper details how the programmatic aspects of the projects were adapted to be recorded and tracked in the ISM.

results.title: Creating Future Space Technology Workforce Utilizing CubeSat Platforms: Challenges, Good Practices, and Lessons Learned
results.abstract: View Video Presentation: https://doi.org/10.2514/6.2021-1437.vidThe United States Naval Academy?s Small Satellite Program (NASSP) has been actively developing and launching space payloads since 2001 and has involved hundreds of undergraduate students in the design, development, integration, testing, and operation aspects of space systems engineering. NASSP has launched 17 space payloads so far, including seven CubeSats, with two more manifested for launch in 2021. The Naval Academy is an undergraduate-only institution, and thus has fostered a satellite engineering program centered around projects that were purely managed and run by students. NASSP and its space system projects have become more mature and streamlined over the years where the current Capstone Design operation is very close to achieving a ?One CubeSat a Year? model. The goal is to realize a streamlined design curriculum where the students will be able to experience the entire scope of a satellite system project cycle, from concept design to launch and operation. This paper will describe the challenges that such a program faces, discuss good practices learned along the way, and detail some lessons learned.

results.title: A scheduling optimization using greedy knapsack algorithm for RANDEV CubeSat communication and observation missions analyzed with MBSE Activity Diagram
results.abstract: Repeater Arrangement & Disaster Early View (RANDEV) is a 3U CubeSat whose payloads are hyper-spectral camera, S-band receiver, and X-band transmitter. RANDEV conducts an earth observation mission to collect potential hazard image data from volcanoes, coasts, and clouds. The antennas are used to conduct store & forward and satellite internet missions. The concept of operations (CONOPS) of RANDEV is organized using top-down approach, and the top of the CONOPS is defined to ?Operation? which is comprised of ?Modes?. A Mode consist of ?Behaviors?, and they are composed of ?Actions?. The Actions are the bottom of the RANDEV missions, and defined by SysML Activity Diagram in language. The Actions are function names of RANDEV subsystem softwares. The time consumption of software functions is estimated using the activity diagram, and in order to practice three missions, a time scheduling methodology is proposed using greedy-knapsack algorithm in this research.
